- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next period.
- When sentiment is negative (≤0.33) or volatile, model often underestimates; increase forecast by 1–3% to compensate for downward bias.
- After a sharp price spike (forecast > true by >5%), model frequently overcorrects; reduce subsequent forecast by 2–5% to avoid overshoot.
- If true outcome shows mean reversion (price drops after peak or rises after trough), model often fails to adjust; align forecast with 3–5 day moving average of history.
- For 30-day horizon, model tends to overreact to sentiment shifts; apply sentiment-weighted smoothing: if sentiment >0.67, use 70% history + 30% forecast; if sentiment <0.33, use 30% history + 70% forecast.
- When sentiment history shows alternating highs/lows (e.g., 0.67, 0.33, 0.67), model often misreads trend; use sentiment momentum (last 3 sentiment values) to adjust forecast direction.
